one_line_reason: The only human oral-intake record involving actual papaya material (papain) tests it only as part of a 3-enzyme blend in cancer patients and concludes evidence is insufficient; every other human trial in the shortlist uses papaya LEAF, not fruit/papain.

selected.population: cancer patients across GI, gynecologic, head-and-neck, lung, and hematologic malignancies (systematic review, 15 studies, 3008 patients)
selected.intervention: oral proteolytic enzyme therapy including papain (derived from papaya) combined with bromelain and chymotrypsin, alongside conventional cancer therapy
selected.primary_outcome: side-effects of anticancer therapy, quality of life, anticancer effects, survival
selected.why_selected: the only shortlisted record where humans actually ingest a papaya-derived compound (papain), though only as part of a multi-enzyme blend, and the review concludes evidence is insufficient to attribute a clear benefit.

blockers: Papain is combined with bromelain and chymotrypsin in every study reviewed; no trial isolates papaya-derived papain alone.

The population studied is cancer patients receiving concurrent conventional anticancer therapy, not general supplement users, and the review's own conclusion is that evidence is insufficient to show a clear benefit.

Every other human record in this shortlist tests papaya LEAF (for chemotherapy/dengue-related thrombocytopenia, or as a galactagogue) rather than the fruit or its papain enzyme, an important plant-part mismatch for this catalog identity.

excluded_pmids.reason: Agricultural/horticultural systematic review of tropical fruit crop research trends in the Mediterranean Basin; not a human health study.
Meta-analysis of Carica papaya LEAF extract (CPLE) for chemotherapy-induced thrombocytopenia, combining human and animal data; wrong plant part.
Bibliometric/ethnobotanical review of plant use in Nigeria; Carica papaya mentioned only as a frequently-cited species with no specific human efficacy trial data.
Systematic review of dengue treatments; Carica papaya LEAF extract combined with doxycycline; wrong plant part and a combination product.
In vitro study of silver nanoparticles synthesized using plant extracts (including papaya) for antibacterial testing; not a human supplement exposure.
Meta-analysis of Carica papaya (leaf) extract for dengue; wrong plant part, and concludes current evidence is insufficient.
Ethnopharmacology review of anti-Buruli-ulcer plants; Carica papaya mentioned only generally among many plants without clear plant-part or route detail.
Narrative ethnobotanical review of medicinal plants for women's healthcare; no specific Carica papaya trial data given.
Review of herbal antioxidant sources; the Carica papaya finding cited is from an animal study, not a human trial.

RCT of a polyherbal galactagogue containing papaya LEAVES (not fruit) as one of three herbs, compared against a single-herb commercial product that does not even contain papaya; wrong plant part, combination product, and no arm isolating papaya's own effect.
Fermented papaya combined with fermented mangosteen in a topical shampoo/lotion for hair loss; a topical cosmetic application, not an oral supplement, and a combination product.
